argument.text: Use H001. For E002 take arbitrary I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1 and lambda=0 for the X estimate. X gives precisely L-infinity L2 and L-infinity H^(-23/14) derivative, its hypotheses. Its three choices of negative-norm slot are retained. For constant inputs use E002 with any lambda in [0,1]. Each source spatial norm is sqrt(2 pi) times ours: divide by sqrt(2 pi) on the output and absorb the remaining product factors 2 pi into the constant. This proves the first two assertions without changing their exponent or time length. Smooth or continuous piecewise smooth time functions have the stated distributional derivative, so E002 applies directly. General X inputs use the source bounded interpretation of the operator. When a=b the integral is zero, so the zero-length interval case follows directly. The negative spatial norm is finite for X inputs: since <k>>=1, the weights <k>^(-2pstar) are at most 1, and termwise comparison of D003's nonnegative squared Fourier sums gives ||h||_{H^(-pstar)}<=||h||_2, also in time L-infinity. D019 supplies the bounded extension interpretation, and D020 supplies the distributional derivative for continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs.

produces.statement: For every I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1 and fj in X(I), ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||fj||_X+C||fi||_{L-infinity H^(-pstar)} product_{j!=i}||fj||_{L-infinity L2}, for each i in {1,2,3}. For time-independent fj in H^lambda and 0<=lambda<=1, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda |I|^lambda product_j||fj||_{H^lambda}; at |I|=0 the integral is zero. Constants are uniform in interval location and support, and the bounded interpretation agrees with smooth inputs.

argument.text: H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply the product inequality in E003 with lambda=gamma and, when gamma=1/2, epsilon=1/8. This is permitted because 1/8>0 and the product inequality allows any fixed positive epsilon. The source exponent a(lambda) is exactly a_gamma by its definition. Consequently ||fg||_2<=C_gamma ||f||_{H^gamma}||g||_{H^{a_gamma}} for arbitrary f in H^gamma and g in H^{a_gamma}. Dividing by sqrt(2 pi) converts the source output norm to the D003 norm and leaves just the fixed factor sqrt(2 pi) on the right, absorbed into C_gamma. For the stage estimate at lambda=1/2, the phrase 'arbitrary fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0' in E003 asserts a positive threshold such that every smaller positive loss is admissible. There is a positive loss below both this threshold and 1/8: take half the smaller of these two positive numbers. E003 therefore gives the existence of a real stageLossLocal in (0,1/8] such that, for every beta in [-1/2-stageLossLocal,3/2], every mean-zero time-independent q1,q2 in H^{1/2}, t_n>=0, tau>0 and t in [t_n,t_n+tau], the source norms satisfy ||(1/2) integral_{t_n}^t B_s(q1,q2) ds||_{H^beta}<=C_{beta,stageLossLocal} tau^((3/2-beta)/(2+stageLossLocal)) ||q1||_{H^{1/2}}||q2||_{H^{1/2}}. The constants depend only on beta and the loss. This loss can be chosen independently of the step and input data.

produces.statement: There exists a real stageLossLocal with 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8 such that for all mean-zero time-independent q1,q2 in H^{1/2}, every t_n>=0, tau>0, t in [t_n,t_n+tau], and beta in [-1/2-stageLossLocal,3/2], one has ||(1/2) integral_{t_n}^t B_s(q1,q2) ds||_{H^beta} <= C_{beta,stageLossLocal} tau^((3/2-beta)/(2+stageLossLocal)) ||q1||_{H^{1/2}}||q2||_{H^{1/2}}, using source unnormalized norms. The constant depends only on beta and stageLossLocal, and is uniform in the inputs, step location, step size, step time and Fourier support.

For every productLeftLocal in H^gamma and productRightLocal in H^{a_gamma}, ||productLeftLocal productRightLocal||_2<=C_gamma ||productLeftLocal||_{H^gamma}||productRightLocal||_{H^{a_gamma}}, in the normalized Fourier Sobolev norms, with a constant depending only on gamma and the fixed product loss 1/8 at gamma=1/2.

argument.text:
Choose stageLossLocal as in F002, once and independently of all step data. Fix arbitrary mean-zero w in H^gamma, a bound ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1 and t in I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], retaining these antecedents throughout the conclusion. Since gamma>0, comparison of the D003 Fourier weights gives ||w||_2<=||w||_{H^gamma}, so the inputs also lie in the domain of B. In E003 take lambda=gamma and f1=f2=w. Only in the middle stage case substitute the source loss epsilon=stageLossLocal. By D022 the resulting diagonal stage G_n(t;w,w) equals F_n(t;w), because their defining integrals coincide. Define beta0=2gamma-3/2 if gamma<1/2, -1/2-stageLossLocal if gamma=1/2, and gamma-1 if gamma>1/2. For beta selected as a_gamma or 1+gamma put theta=(1+gamma-beta)/(1+gamma-beta0).
For beta=a_gamma, the range condition and exponent comparison follow case by case. If 0<gamma<1/2, then a_gamma-beta0=2-3gamma>0 and 1+gamma-a_gamma=1/2+2gamma>0. The denominator is 5/2-gamma>0 and theta=(1/2+2gamma)/(5/2-gamma). The inequality theta>=gamma follows from gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2=(gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0. If gamma=1/2, then a_gamma remains 1/8, a_gamma-beta0=5/8+stageLossLocal>0 and 1+gamma-a_gamma=11/8>0. The denominator is 2+stageLossLocal, and theta=(11/8)/(2+stageLossLocal)=11/(16+8eta)>=11/17>1/2, since 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8. Thus this calculation uses the fixed target regularity 1/8 and the separately chosen admissible source loss stageLossLocal. If 1/2<gamma<=1, then a_gamma=0>=gamma-1=beta0, a_gamma<=1+gamma, the denominator is 2 and theta=(1+gamma)/2>=gamma. These exhaustive cases verify beta in [beta0,1+gamma] and theta>=gamma. E003 therefore gives ||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{a_gamma}}<=C tau^theta ||w||_{H^gamma}^2. Here and below constants are converted to our normalization: dividing each bilinear source estimate by sqrt(2 pi) leaves just the fixed factor sqrt(2 pi), absorbed into C. Because 0<tau<=1 and theta>=gamma, tau^theta=tau^gamma tau^(theta-gamma)<=tau^gamma. Also the norm antecedent implies M>=0 and ||w||_{H^gamma}^2<=M^2. Hence ||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{a_gamma}}<=C_M tau^gamma uniformly in t.
For beta=1+gamma the same source hypotheses hold. In the three cases the positive denominators 1+gamma-beta0 are respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+stageLossLocal and 2; beta is the upper endpoint, so theta=0. E003 gives ||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{1+gamma}}<=C ||w||_{H^gamma}^2<=C_M uniformly in t. Taking the supremum over I_n gives both asserted stage estimates. The fixed stageLossLocal can affect the constants but, being selected once from E003 at lambda=1/2, introduces no dependence on w, t_n, tau, t or Fourier support. All uses require only the stipulated H^gamma regularity. Universal introduction under the retained antecedents proves the stage clauses; together with F001 and F003 these prove the full asserted conclusion, with all stated uniformity and extension properties.

value.type: compact additive group with normalized measure
value.definition: torus=ℝ/(2πℤ), written \mathbb T in formulas; integration uses dx/(2π). The parameter T denotes the time horizon.

value.type: Fourier coefficient map on the torus
value.definition: For integrable f, Fourier(f)(k) = fhat(k) = (2 pi)^(-1) integral_0^{2 pi} f(x) exp(-ikx) dx; extend by distributional duality.

For real s, H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with norm squared sum_{k in Z} <k>^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are distributions. L2=H^0 with normalized measure. On mean-zero distributions dot H^s has squared norm sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2. Smooth means spatially C-infinity. Real means fhat(-k)=conjugate(fhat(k)), and mean-zero means fhat(0)=0. Sequence ell2 uses counting measure. Time L-infinity norms are essential suprema, except time suprema of continuous representatives. Generic constants C may change; C_M depends only on gamma,T,M, never on a Fourier support bound or timestep.

value.type: Airy group indexed by real times
value.definition: S_t = exp(-t partial_x^3); Fourier(S_t f)(k)= exp(it k^3) fhat(k).
P0 f=fhat(0), as a constant function.
P=I-P0; the identity operator is I.

value.type: inverse spatial derivative with zero mode removed
value.definition: Dinv=partial_x^(-1)=D^(-1), Fourier multiplier (ik)^(-1) at nonzero k and zero at k=0.

value.type: time-integrated trilinear operator initially on smooth inputs
value.definition: C_I(f,g,h)= integral_I S_{-t}P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)](S_t Dinv h)} dt. For lower regularity its meaning is the bounded extension supplied by the continuous estimates.

For compact interval I, ||f||_{X(I)}=||f||_{L-infinity(I;L2)}+||partial_t f||_{L-infinity(I;H^(-pstar))}, using the distributional time derivative. Subintervals use the same continuous representatives; piecewise smooth continuous functions have this distributional derivative almost everywhere.
a_gamma=1/2-gamma if 0<gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 if 1/2<gamma<=1.
For time-independent mean-zero f and t in I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], F_n(t;f)=1/2 integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f,f) ds. Write F_n(t)=F_n(t;f) when f is fixed.

A type explicitly named natural numbers, integers, rationals, reals or complex numbers means that standard structure, with its usual numerals and arithmetic operations; these operation tokens need not be redeclared as project objects. The fixed finite calculation rules below, including a+0=a, are controller permissions, not an author claim. The core symbol table below is not a dictionary of all allowed mathematics. Objects and notation from any subject are introduced by this problem's parameters, D definitions or scoped locals, with their types and dependencies. Their properties need direct inputs or displayed local proofs; a familiar name or symbol supplies no theorem.

1: # Audit A: mathematical review in Yui
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `yui-nl0-audit-a-2`.
7: 
8: The author and independent auditor use this same mathematical standard. NL0
9: reviews a complete natural-language proof and necessary mathematical detail.
10: Specific Lean declarations, signatures, representations and proof tactics are
11: implementation work for nl02lean, not prerequisites for ordinary NL0 review.
12: The following grouped criteria replace V1's ten separate per-R report rows.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the complete original theorem, every original H, quantifier, domain, normalization and supplied core proof route. A parameter or definition cannot hide a hypothesis or desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | declaration_check | Define mathematical objects and notation sufficiently for their actual uses. Check types, dependencies, construction guards and legitimate local introductions. A definition grants no unproved property. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Check complete E statements, primary-source identity, context and conditions under the source policy. An explicitly selected native M retains its bound signature checks; authors need not introduce M nodes for ordinary mathematical background. Unavailable originals remain disclosed UNVERIFIED source assumptions. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | Verify the actual AND dependency graph, unique producers, absence of cycles and faithful exported statements. Retain every original H and disclose unused H. Internal results are proved, never new roots. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Inputs and output state the mathematical content, objects, domains, quantifiers and conditions their consumers need. Check actual object occurrences and definitions. No missing identification can be supplied by an absent producer proof or a paper equation number. |
21: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Check direct input use, earlier local facts, witness existence and proper discharge of assumptions. No circular dependency, future fact or escaped local object is allowed. Mathematically checked routine background may supplement the packet without prior native lookup. |
22: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Verify the complete implication and every output clause at ordinary rigorous mathematical granularity, including material limiting operations, domains and regularity. Compress correct routine reasoning; locate a real gap rather than requiring a transcript of elementary steps. |
23: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | Check actual instantiations and all material premises of invoked E/M or routine background facts, with grounds in inputs or earlier local derivations. Required bridges are proved. A familiar theorem name or a proposed Lean tactic supplies no mathematical justification. |
24: 
25: ### Scope and mathematical boundary
26: 
27: Global review owns target/H fidelity, definitions, source statements and graph
28: consistency. Each local reviewer owns the conditional implication at its R
29: node. Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary: these statements are conditional premises.
30: The local reviewer does not re-prove an input N or re-audit its source paper;
31: the graph and that producer's review establish those separate obligations.
32: Conversely, an input N exports only its full statement, not unexported facts
33: from the producer's body. The fifth local criterion, packet_replay, assesses
34: sufficiency under this exact boundary. The controller records execution
35: identity and exposure independently of the mathematical judgment.
36: 
37: Review correctness rather than the number of displayed lines. Ordinary valid
38: textbook compression is allowed. Material missing hypotheses, witnesses,
39: constructions, scope discharges or core arguments are not implementation gaps.
40: Return them for located author repair and fresh review. No theorem needs to be re-proved
41: when its legitimate mathematical source and actual application suffice.
42: 
43: The domain-neutral elementary-language-4 profile retains equality, supplied
44: definitions, finite arithmetic/order reasoning and finite sums. It is syntax
45: and elementary calculation policy, not a subject vocabulary or theorem list.
46: Objects from any field use problem parameters, D definitions or scoped locals.
47: Neither an author-written calculation list nor a familiar symbol adds a theorem.
48: 
49: ### Mathematical background: mathematical-background-v2-1
50: 
51: A reviewer may positively assess a routine, local mathematical fact without
52: first finding its Mathlib declaration. Record its precise mathematical
53: statement, actual argument location, available condition grounds and a short
54: mathematical justification in a background note. Use kind mathematical for an
55: ordinary background result and elementary for a useful elementary completion.
56: This is an actual mathematical judgment, not a future TODO or a claim of
57: native verification. Do not record every algebraic operation.
58: 
59: Eligibility requires a correct standard local step with all premises already
60: available, no new H and no substantial new core proof or changed route.
61: Important external tools remain explicit E inputs; a missing project result
62: or uncertain source cannot be waived as background. If an explicitly supplied
63: native mathlib note is retained, its full bound evidence is still validated.
64: No field-specific whitelist determines eligibility.
65: 
66: The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus its hash-bound mathematical
67: review supplement. It is a natural-language audit under the mathematical-background policy, not a
68: detailed-NL0 format-3 native-background receipt. At nl02lean, workers must discharge all necessary
69: facts by actual Lean proofs or checked library use; a note never becomes an
70: unproved H, axiom or extra external assumption. The exact implementation may
71: differ while preserving the mathematical meaning.
72: 
73: ### Actual review and result qualification
74: 
75: Independent reviewers assess the actual content; schema validation does not
76: prove mathematics. An unexamined item remains unread/read. A mathematical
77: uncertainty is assessed UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Missing or conflicting assessments
78: block acceptance. Ordinary source-access deferral follows the conditional-source
79: policy and must appear in final warnings; it cannot yield unqualified PASS.
80: 
81: Use short located reasons for straightforward PASS items and enough detail to
82: make a defect or uncertainty actionable. Avoid duplicate explanations across
83: criteria. A concise report still covers every required mathematical check.
84: Do not read author self-check notes, old verdicts, other R proof bodies, other
85: case results or personal proof skills to manufacture independent approval.
86: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
87: 
88: ## Execution protocol
89: 
90: 1. Freeze the original problem, spec and NL0. A separate fresh global reviewer
91:    reads the exhaustive global-overview.json, relevant canonical content and
92:    source evidence. Review each D and selected E/M; the overview is data, not
93:    an assessment. Do not infer absence from a partial page.
94: 2. Complete global source/graph review before dispatching local R reviews.
95:    Up to the explicitly confirmed N independent R reviewers work concurrently.
96:    Each receives only its own packet and mathematical-NL0 rules. Review full arguments,
97:    actual applications and definitions; input N statements are conditional.
98: 3. Prefer one complete artifact with an explicit coverage map. Use
99:    record_review_item and read_review_progress only for useful checkpoints.
100:    record_background_note is optional; a complete artifact may include its
101:    actual notes directly. Batch reading several declared fragments is available.
102: 4. Each local report has inference, packet_sha256, verdict, notes, checks,
103:    findings and optional background_notes. The checks map contains exactly
104:    statement_closure, dependency_closure, argument, applicability, packet_replay.
105:    Each row has verdict, notes and resolving packet locations. E applications
106:    additionally retain actual binding, per-hypothesis, conclusion and bridge
107:    assessments; this is mathematical applicability, not a Lean API inventory.
108: 5. Global reports have target_review, definition_reviews, source_reviews,
109:    structure_review and findings. Each E adds citation_checks for
110:    literature_identity, result_location, statement_fidelity,
111:    context_completeness, version_and_eligibility. Inaccessible primary text
112:    leaves blocked checks UNVERIFIED while remaining assessment continues.
113: 6. A blocking finding needs its actual location, explanation and a short exact
114:    quotation from that location. Preserve the defect and untouched coverage.
115:    Return located mathematical repairs to the author; review changed scopes
116:    independently. Do not resample a mathematical rejection or silently erase it.
117: 7. The collector checks complete coverage, consistency, exact bytes and actual
118:    independent execution before producing the audit-format-4 receipt.
119:    Old detailed-NL0 format-3 receipts are not silently upgraded. Inherited format-4 judgments retain
120:    their original source/rule hashes, exposure and costs.
121: 
122: ## Sources, scopes and final handoff
123: 
124: Use [external theorem review](external-theorems.md) and
125: [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md) for source identity, exact
126: statements and warnings. Reuse adequate original text; several theorem uses
127: may share one staged readback. Each application still discharges its own
128: premises. No successful download or guessed Mathlib availability is approval.
129: 
130: Use [logical rules](logical-rules.md) for local scopes and
131: [background notes](background-notes.md) for the mathematical supplement.
132: The ordinary complete result remains relative to explicit E assumptions.
133: An inaccessible E original permits only a source-qualified result. Translation
134: retains this exact audit and supplement until reviewed mathematical changes
135: invalidate affected scopes. Typed interfaces, native checking, standalone
136: assembly and independent semantic Audit B are separate later gates.
137: 
138: ## Paywalled or inaccessible primary text
139: 
140: Follow [conditional sources](conditional-sources.md). Preserve the complete
141: secondary statement and actual access evidence; unavailable source checks
142: stay UNVERIFIED. Continue other work only with an explicitly qualified source
143: assumption, and report warn.json/warn.md. No unqualified full PASS is granted.

artifact.notes: The current packet proves N005 conditionally on H001, E002 and E003. F002 legitimately extracts one sufficiently small admissible stage loss, fixed independently of the data; S003 uses it while retaining target regularity a_gamma=1/8. All five supplied applications, norm conversions, exponent ranges, supremum bounds and local witness discharges have been assessed. The stray token 'eta' in one redundant arithmetic rewrite in S003 is a typographical slip: BG003 records the correct calculation directly from the preceding expression and the actual bound on stageLossLocal. No hypothesis or mathematical object is inferred from that token. Source-paper identity and execution attestation remain outside this conditional mathematical judgment.

applicability.notes: E002 applies at lambda=0 to X inputs and at arbitrary lambda in [0,1] to constant H^lambda inputs. E003's product loss 1/8 is permitted, and F002 supplies an admissible sufficiently small stage loss for A003/A004. All interval, mean-zero, derivative and beta-range premises are available; all five applications are reviewed below.

argument.notes: S001 establishes both trilinear bounds with the supplied bounded interpretation and zero-length case. S002 proves the product estimate and the loss witness. S003 verifies all three beta/theta cases, obtains theta>=gamma at beta=a_gamma and theta=0 at beta=1+gamma, uses 0<tau<=1 and ||w||<=M, and takes the uniform time supremum. Cubic and bilinear normalization factors are respectively 2 pi and sqrt(2 pi); all constant dependencies are retained. The redundant 'eta' rewrite is resolved by BG003, without changing the argument.

dependency_closure.notes: Only H001, E002, E003, supplied definitions, earlier F001/F002/F003 and the routine notes below are used. F002 follows by selecting half the smaller of the positive source threshold and 1/8. Its existential witness is chosen in S003 once for all data; it has no escaping identity or data-dependent constant. Arbitrary step/input antecedents remain in the exported clauses. H001's gamma restriction is used; T>0 and R>0 are unused. There are no circular or future dependencies.

packet_replay.notes: The supplied current statements, definitions and in-scope local facts suffice for this implication. In particular the sufficiently-small-loss quantifier is explicitly instantiated through F002, rather than supplemented by source-paper knowledge or a different proof. No producer body, absent project result, or earlier verdict is used as a premise.

statement_closure.notes: N005 supplies the norm inequalities, domains, slot and exponent quantifiers, step and interval restrictions, zero-length convention, bounded-extension meaning and uniformity. D019/D020 define the trilinear operator and X; D021/D022 identify the target regularity and diagonal stage. Local witness and product losses have distinct scopes, and F002's quantified statement exports its full meaning. The isolated 'eta' token in S003 is dispensable to the derivation: BG003 proves the intended inequality entirely using the already defined stageLossLocal; no exported statement contains eta.

A001.notes: Direct lambda=0 specialization of the first trilinear estimate, retaining all three negative-norm slots.

bindings_review.notes: lambda=0, [a,b]=I and the three given X(I) inputs match E002. D016 gives pstar=23/14.

hypothesis_reviews.notes: The arbitrary interval retains 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1; 0 belongs to [0,1].

D020's X norm supplies L-infinity L2 regularity and a bounded distributional H^(-23/14) derivative. S001 also verifies finiteness of the negative input norm by the Fourier weights. Continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs satisfying these bounds have no jump contribution to their distributional derivative, as recorded in BG002.

conclusion_review.notes: With c=sqrt(2 pi), dividing both cubic terms by the output scaling c leaves c^2=2 pi, absorbed into C. The |I| power, all slot choices, location/support uniformity and D019 bounded interpretation are retained; the singleton integral is zero.

A002.notes: The product clause expressly permits any fixed positive loss at lambda=1/2.

bindings_review.notes: lambda=gamma and epsilon=1/8 at the middle case make a(lambda)=a_gamma in all three cases; the inputs are the arbitrary f and g.

hypothesis_reviews.notes: H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. The product clause requires only a fixed positive middle-case loss, so 1/8 is admissible for this clause.
The input spaces are exactly H^gamma and H^{a_gamma}. Stage-only mean-zero, step and beta hypotheses are irrelevant to the product clause.

conclusion_review.notes: The source bilinear inequality becomes F003 and the product clause of N005 after division by c=sqrt(2 pi), leaving just c in the constant. Dependence is only on gamma and the fixed product loss.

A003.notes: The stage uses a fixed admissible source loss from F002, independently of the target regularity at gamma=1/2.

bindings_review.notes: lambda=gamma, f1=f2=w and beta=a_gamma identify G_n(t;w,w)=F_n(t;w) by the identical half-integrals. At gamma=1/2 the source epsilon is stageLossLocal, while beta stays 1/8.

hypothesis_reviews.notes: H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. S002 interprets sufficiently small as a positive threshold and chooses half the minimum with 1/8, proving F002. The witness chosen in S003 thus satisfies 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8 and source admissibility, with no dependence on w or the step.

w is time-independent, mean-zero and in H^gamma, with t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1 and t in I_n. Fourier-weight comparison puts w in L2 for D017. For beta=a_gamma the lower-end gaps are 2-3gamma>0, 5/8+stageLossLocal>0 and 1-gamma>=0. The corresponding upper-end gaps are positive. Hence beta0<=beta<=1+gamma in every case.

conclusion_review.notes: The time exponents are (1/2+2gamma)/(5/2-gamma), (11/8)/(2+stageLossLocal), and (1+gamma)/2. The stated quadratic calculation and loss bound imply theta>=gamma, including the precise middle-case calculation in BG003. The source estimate, bilinear normalization, tau^theta<=tau^gamma and ||w||^2<=M^2 give the asserted supremum bound with constants uniform in step and support.

A004.notes: The upper endpoint stage uses the same fixed admissible loss, with exponent zero.

bindings_review.notes: lambda=gamma, f1=f2=w and beta=1+gamma select the upper endpoint for F_n. At gamma=1/2 the source loss is the witness stageLossLocal from F002.

hypothesis_reviews.notes: The gamma range follows from H001. At gamma=1/2 source admissibility follows from S002's threshold construction and F002, using the same once-fixed witness in S003.

The same mean-zero time-independent H^gamma input and nonnegative-start positive-length step meet the source conditions. beta is the upper endpoint, and 1+gamma-beta0 equals respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+stageLossLocal or 2, all positive.

conclusion_review.notes: The numerator 1+gamma-beta vanishes, so tau^theta=1. Dividing the bilinear source bound by sqrt(2 pi), absorbing the remaining fixed factor, using ||w||<=M and taking the uniform supremum gives exactly the H^{1+gamma} clause. The fixed source-loss choice does not add data dependence to C_M.

A005.notes: The constant-input clause applies for the entire specified exponent interval.

bindings_review.notes: The arbitrary lambda in [0,1], [a,b]=I and three constant H^lambda inputs match E002's second clause.

hypothesis_reviews.notes: The arbitrary interval satisfies 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1, and lambda is in [0,1].
The inputs are time-independent in H^lambda, so their distributional derivatives are zero. The case a=b is handled separately by the zero integral.

conclusion_review.notes: The trilinear norm conversion leaves only c^2=2 pi in the constant and preserves |I|^lambda and all uniformity. Thus the second trilinear clause of N005 follows, including its separate zero-length convention.

background_notes.fact: For 0<tau<=1 and real theta>=gamma, tau^theta<=tau^gamma. A pointwise bound uniform for all t in I_n remains a bound on the supremum over I_n.

grounds.reason: The arbitrary step is in (0,1].
S003 derives theta>=gamma and gives estimates uniform in the step time t.

background_notes.justification: Since log tau<=0, exp((theta-gamma)log tau)<=1. Multiplying by tau^gamma yields the inequality. A common upper bound for all values in a set is an upper bound for its supremum. This is exactly the uniform-bound passage in S003.

background_notes.fact: A continuous time-dependent function that is C1 on each piece of a finite partition, with its piecewise derivative bounded in H^(-pstar), has distributional time derivative equal almost everywhere to that piecewise derivative; there are no Dirac masses at the partition points. Thus continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs with the stated X bounds meet E002's derivative premise.

grounds.reason: X is defined using distributional derivatives and the continuous piecewise time-smooth class is explicitly specified.
S001 applies the source estimate to that continuous piecewise class under the stated X regularity.

background_notes.justification: Test against a compactly supported smooth scalar time function and a spatial smooth test function, integrate by parts on each smooth time piece, and sum. Continuity cancels the boundary terms at every common partition point; the exterior terms vanish by compact support. The remaining integrals are exactly the piecewise derivative pairing, with the assumed H^(-pstar) bound.

background_notes.fact: If 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8, then (11/8)/(2+stageLossLocal)=11/(16+8 stageLossLocal)>=11/17>1/2. This proves S003's middle-case exponent comparison directly from its correctly defined expression, without using the isolated unbound token 'eta' in the redundant intervening rewrite.

grounds.reason: F002 provides 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8.
S003 chooses precisely that witness.
The middle-case exponent is explicitly (11/8)/(2+stageLossLocal), since beta=1/8 and gamma=1/2.

background_notes.justification: The denominator 16+8 stageLossLocal is positive and at most 17. Dividing the positive numerator 11 by these denominators gives the weak inequality; 11/17>1/2 is equivalent to 22>17. The equality is finite field arithmetic. This is a routine local correction of a dispensable displayed token, with no new assumption, witness or proof route.
